discipline: Cartography and information design. AI-written; read-only (nothing changed, written or run beyond small python reads of /Users/ren/theories/tmp/r7/places/*.json and theories/becoming/results/atlas/entries/{dynamics,premises,situations}.json). Classifications of the 88 decisions below are my reading of the decisions' own notes, not a re-check against the Lean.
verdict_on_present:
Right, and worth keeping: places named by what is happening; every mark settled against a Lean statement and put to a refuter; strength as line style; the unplaced kept (12 unresolved, 7 leads-out); and the one empirical fact we have, that Ren looked for five minutes and said it is the kind of map he meant. Boxes with names and lines between them read as a map; keep that look.

Dominated as a data structure, in two ways that the decisions file already documents in its prose notes. (1) The place is stored as a primitive, but the 15 places are combinations of a few independent distinctions (where the rule comes from; whether what leads is held; whether what is used up reaches anyone with a say; whether in time; whether the rule goes by it). Overlap, containment and 'the same change seen from two overlapping places' therefore cannot be stored or drawn, only said in glosses. (2) The arrow is stored as a primitive, but one arrow glyph carries five different things: a dividing line, a fork on one comparison, a change that needs the set-up altered from outside, a law of the course itself, and a single built example. A reader takes all 38 as 'this tends to lead there'; by my count from the notes only 7 of the 38 are that.

So the present structure is not on the frontier: a structure that stores the distinctions and types the marks is at least as good on five-minute reading (same named places, fewer arrows) and better on faithfulness, economy at 434 items, use on a real case, and scaling. Whether it is better in five minutes for a person is untested and I say so below.
dominated_where: One glyph, five kinds. Of the 38 arrows (my classification from the notes in decisions.json): 9 are dividing lines stated both ways (shaping tr 1,2,4,5; shaping-read tr 2; offspring tr 1,2; unselected exits 1,6: 'a boundary, not a passage in time'); 6 are heads of comparisons that fork (readers-drawn exit 1 + tr 2 are ONE law, Thinned.kept_iff, drawn as two arrows to two places; loss-read-in-time exit 1 + tr 1; shaping-read exit 1; reading-a-loss-in-time tr 1, whose second head sits in a note); 7 happen only if something the law takes as given is changed from outside (closed-capture exits 1,2 and a-counter-rule exit 2: 'a change of how the rule is rebuilt, not a change of the counts'; selection-read-off exit 1: 'a comparison of two ways of taking the measure, not a movement in time'; a-code exit 2; unselected exits 2,3); 7 are laws of the course (a-code exit 1; shaping-read exit 2; loss-read tr 2; reading-a-loss exits 1,2; selection-read-off exit 4; what-an-optimum tr 1); 6 are single built examples; 3 are readings.

What a person wrongly takes away. Eight arrows enter 'The cost counts' from four boxes. None is the loop doing it: three are re-settings of the rule from outside (one theorem, ClosedCapture.turned_by_loss, drawn from two origin places), one is a different way of taking the measure, three are one side of a count taken at the moment someone already objects (and the note on shaping-read exit 1 says 'no law gives holds-itself -> felt'), one is a single example. The picture says 'capture tends toward the cost counting'; the laws say nothing inside the loop goes there.

Overlap cannot be stored. 'Judged only from inside' is 'holds itself' plus something not counted, but that exists only in gloss prose. Consequences in the data: holds-itself's test has to say 'the law says NOTHING about a loss' to keep the two apart; the same theorem appears as arrows from judged-inside and from holds-itself; the checkers report further overlaps the list cannot hold (shaping-pays with holds-itself above the tipping count; noticers-gone with all-on-one, 'one fact said two ways'; felt with past-turning-back).

The tests sort theorems, not situations. 12 of the 15 place tests are worded about the law ('The law says…', 'the law concerns…', 'no law in play', 'No law'). A person with a real fishery or a real training pipeline cannot apply 'the law does not yet say the rule has turned'. So the map cannot be used to find a case, and situations.json's one case has no link to any place.

Position carries nothing. layout.json is 15 hand-set coordinates. The plane, the strongest thing a map has, encodes no relation; left-to-right and 'The cost counts' top right read as progress to a good end, which is the dualism Ren objects to, produced by layout alone. At 35-40 places and about 150 arrows a hand-set node-link drawing is a tangle and cannot be regenerated when a place is added.

The most exact knowledge is off the picture and the least exact is on it. 16 items are 'inside' notes in panels, among them four exact thresholds (the tipping counts of capture-by-counted-choices tr 1 and shaping-read tr 1, 4; readers-drawn tr 1), while 8 single built examples are drawn as arrows.

Growth is linear in places. 19 of 88 items (22%) got no mark, several because a place is missing ('rebuilt but not yet held', 'made good again', 'the loss falls on the winners themselves', 'what a shared way can no longer tell apart'). Each fix is one more place. the-lock exit 3 shows the cost: the rule turns although nobody noticed the loss, a combination cost-counts' test forbids ('BECAUSE the loss is read'), so it 'leads out'; as a combination of two answers it needs no new place.

Family E's items were forced onto 'Bending the rule costs/pays' (offspring tr 1, 2) with the checker noting that giving back and forgiving a slip are not what anyone would call bending the rule. The shared thing is the comparison, not the place.
proposal_in_one_paragraph: Store the distinctions the laws actually draw, not the places and not the arrows. A QUESTION is one distinction with two or three answers, worded as a comparison wherever the law compares ('which is more: what comes back to those who bend the rule, or what it costs them?'), asked of someone named. A PLACE is a short named set of answers and nothing else; overlap, containment and neighbours are computed. Each atlas item becomes one MARK on one question, of one of four kinds: a line (which side holds; nothing moves), stays, moves (the course itself changes the answer), re-set (the answer changes only if something the law takes as given is changed). A Lean witness and a real situation are the same type, a CASE: a row of answers, built or actual, with 'not known' allowed. Two things are drawn from this one store: a chart on which position means the answers (two chains of questions as the axes, places as rectangles of cells that can nest and abut, lines drawn on shared borders, arrows only for moves and re-sets, cases as dots), and a case sheet (the same questions in order, each answer followed by what the laws say then), which is at once the article for a place and the questionnaire for a real case. This follows the method chapter's own sentence, 'Distinctions state their basis… drawn within the unfolding, along relations, together with what they leave out': the stored unit is the distinction, and a place is a name that points at a few of them.
schema:
question
- id.
- ask: one plain sentence; a comparison ('which is more / which comes first') where the law compares two quantities or two moments.
- of: whom or what it is asked of (the rule, those ahead, those with a say, a dependant, a costly practice). These are the roles situations.json already has.
- answers: two or three, each named by what happens; none named as the better one.
- after: the questions that must be answered before this one makes sense. Gives reading order and the chart's axes.

place
- id, label (en, zh), example.
- answers: {question: answer} for the few questions it fixes; silent on the rest. Nothing else is stored. 'Overlaps', 'is a case of' and 'next to' are computed from this.

mark (one per atlas item; replaces arrow / stays / inside / leads-out)
- item: dynamic and exit, transition or compose number. law: the Lean name.
- on: the one question whose answer it speaks of.
- kind: line (says which side holds, exactly or sufficiently; nothing moves) | stays (the course keeps the answer) | moves (the course itself changes it) | re-set (it changes only if something the law takes as given is changed: who has a say, how the rule is made, how the measure is taken).
- given: {question: answer} that the law's premises fix. Its extent is how far the mark is drawn.
- from, to: answers.
- strength: as now (exact, sufficient, necessary, reading, open). 'Witness' leaves this scale: a witness is a case.
- within: the count of steps, where the law gives one. tie: which side the equal case falls on. condition (en, zh): at most twenty words.

case
- id; built (a Lean witness) or actual (a situation).
- roles: who is the rule, those ahead, those with a say, and so on (from the situation's web).
- answers: {question: answer | not known | not said}; then: the answers afterwards, for a built case that moved.
- source.

In it: a place is a named set of answers. A change is a mark of kind moves or re-set on one question; a line is not a change but where a change would be. A real case is a row of answers with its not-knowns; what can happen next is every mark whose 'given' it meets; what is missing is every question it leaves not known and every border with no mark.
drawn_from_it:
1. THE CHART (the map). For a region, take the two chains of questions (by 'after') that most marks lie on; one runs across, one down. Each cell is a combination of answers. A place is drawn as the labelled rectangle of the cells its answers cover, so places nest and abut instead of floating. For the first region: down = the rule (set from outside / rebuilt from its results, not held / rebuilt and held, with the tipping count as a line inside the last); across = what is used up outside the count (nothing stated / reaches no one with a say / reaches someone, still in time / then two cells side by side: the rule goes by it, too late). 'Holds itself' is the bottom row; 'Drawing on what is not counted' is the second column; 'Judged only from inside' is the cell where they cross. Marks: a line is drawn ON the border between two cells, thick for exact, thin for sufficient or necessary, and only as long as the rows its 'given' covers; a border with no law is left visibly open. Moves: a solid arrow across a border. Re-set: a hollow arrow with a short bar at its tail. Stays: a small tick inside the cell. Case: a dot, hollow for built, filled for actual; two joined dots if a built case moved. Reading: dotted. Questions on neither axis (how many ways are in use; who is among those asked; does it go on, for whom) are small insets in the same grammar, drawn as the islands they are. Click opens the present panel unchanged. Layout is computed from the questions' order; layout.json goes. Whole atlas: one such sheet per region in the same grammar (small multiples), and above them one index table, families down and questions across, a cell filled where the family has marks on that question; families that share a column are thereby joined.

2. THE CASE SHEET. The same questions in 'after' order as one short page. Under each answer: the marks whose 'given' it meets, said in four fixed forms: 'then, by law…' (moves, stays), 'which side: …' (line), 'only if someone changes…' (re-set), 'seen once, in a built example' (case), or 'nothing is shown here'. Filled in with a place's answers it is that place's article. Filled in for an actual case it answers: where is it, what can happen next, what would have to be changed from outside, what is not known.
worked_sample:
Nine questions cover the region (ids are mine; wording to be Ren's):
- rule: where does the rule come from? set from outside | rebuilt from its own results.
- held: does the rule keep ahead what is already ahead? not held | held (inner line: which side of the tipping count).
- pays: a costly practice: which is more, what comes back to its doers or what it costs them? less | at least as much.
- ways: how many ways are in use in the group? several | one.
- reach: something is used up that the rule does not register; does any difference it makes reach someone with a say? nothing stated | reaches no one | reaches someone.
- who: are those it would reach among those asked? among them | not among them.
- time: which comes first, the first moment anyone with a say can tell, or the point after which it cannot be kept? in time | too late.
- turn: does the rule go by it? not yet | the rule no longer favours those it favoured.
- on: does it go on (of whom)? goes on | ended.

SIX PLACES as sets of answers:
- holds-itself = {rule: rebuilt, held: held}. Silent on reach, so the clause 'the law says NOTHING about a loss' is no longer needed.
- judged-inside = {rule: rebuilt, held: held, reach: reaches no one}. Computed: a case of holds-itself; overlaps uncounted. The one law the checkers found in the cell itself: ClosedCapture.lock_outlives_loss.
- uncounted = {reach: reaches no one}. Silent on rule, so it also covers a rule set from outside (what-an-optimum exit 1).
- felt = {reach: reaches someone, time: in time, turn: not yet}.
- past-turning-back = {time: too late}. Silent on reach, which is what loss-read-in-time tr 3 needed ('can be passed before anyone counts the loss').
- cost-counts = {turn: turned}. Silent on reach, so the-lock exit 3 (the rule turns though nobody noticed) is the cell {turn: turned, reach: reaches no one}, not a missing place.
- also: noticers-gone = {who: not among them}; fixed-rule = {rule: set from outside}; shaping-costs and shaping-pays = the two sides of pays.

THE ACTUAL CASE. situations.json's reward-model pipeline, from its own summary: rule: set from outside as written ('in the one pass written no step reads the rule from what it selected'), not said if the pass is repeated; reach: reaches no one ('what the responses do in use… lies beyond the raters' and the reward model's closures'). It is a filled dot in the cell {set from outside, reaches no one}. What the sheet then says: line 1 applies (it would reach someone exactly where something reaching a rater differs); if the reward model is refit on its own outputs the case moves down a row, and that border has no law.

All 38 arrows fall on seven of the nine questions: turn 10, pays 7, ways 7, reach 5, time 4, who 3, on 2.
what_it_reveals:
1. The hole is one step earlier than the flat map shows. The brief's 'no law gives an arrow INTO the hold' is partly an artifact: the list has no place for 'rebuilt from its results but not yet held' (the checkers say so), so RuleCapture.uniform_locks and readers_uniform_locks, which take any start to a held one by the step after the second rebuilding, were filed as 'inside'. With rule and held as separate questions they are moves into the hold. The border with nothing on it is the one before: set from outside to rebuilt from its own results. No item among the 88 is there; target-capture's record says where winners rewrite the rule 'the law says nothing'.

2. The centre's shape, by kind of mark. Into {held, reaches no one}: by the course, sufficient. Staying: sufficient (window_never_read) and necessary (the-lock exit 1). Out along 'turn': only re-sets from outside, or one side of a count taken once someone already counts the loss, which no law produces. That is the concern of AGENTS.md's second paragraph, visible as a pattern of line styles and not as a sentence.

3. A loop between three questions that sits in separate boxes and panels now: held with reach 'no one' (what is used up falls on those who would notice) to who 'not among them' to reach stays 'no one' and held stays. Its legs: the first is one built case and readings (readings-revised exit 4; unselected exit 12 and compose 2; persisting-filters exit 4 was dropped by the refuter); the second is a law (the-lock tr 1, sufficient) and readings (readings-revised exit 6, compose 1; unselected exit 8). So the loop closes on a reading, and the chart shows exactly which leg.

4. How general each law is, as length. The line on reach has no premises and runs the full height. The line on turn runs only in the 'held' row. So 'the general laws stop at reaching someone; whether the rule then turns is known only in named models' is seen, not read in a note.

5. The centre is a crossing. No single law of closed-capture carries judged-inside's whole test (checker's remark): laws live on the row and on the column, one in the cell. A cell where a row and a column cross says that truthfully, and it is less of a thing one falls into.

6. Duplicates and counts. 38 arrows, 34 first-cited laws, seven questions. The picture gets shorter while every item keeps its mark.
loses_or_risks:
- Untested where it matters most. Ren recognised boxes and arrows as a map. A grid of cells may read as a table. I think named rectangles with borders and a few arrows still read as a map, but only a person with the two sheets for five minutes can say. I have shown the present structure is dominated; I have not shown mine is on the frontier.
- Choosing the questions is as much a reading as choosing places. The check available: a question earns its place only if some Lean statement draws that distinction (it has at least one line or stays mark). The nine above are mine from the 15 tests and the notes.
- One question per mark will not always hold. turned_by_loss changes 'turn' and thereby leaves 'held'; family A has a joint threshold. Such items need two marks or stay unresolved. I expect the 12 unresolved to shrink (missing combinations become cells) but not vanish: 'made good again' and 'what a shared way can no longer tell apart' are new questions.
- 'Re-set' can become a new inside/outside dualism. The method chapter says 'Supplied is local: a law supplied to a model need not be external to reality.' The kind must be worded 'outside this law's course', never 'outside the system'; a later law may turn a re-set into a moves, and the mark should then change.
- Yes/no answers can harden into poles. Comparisons with both sides named by what happens help; words such as 'used up' and 'loss' still carry whose loss it is. The 'of' field at least makes 'for whom' a stored fact.
- A chart shows two chains at once. A third needs insets or another sheet; more than three overlapping places in one cell become unreadable. Reading across still suggests progress; the axis order must be stated as 'which question can only be asked after which', not time and not better.
- Path-following across several changes is weaker on a grid than on a node-link drawing; the loop in point 3 needs its own small drawing.

COST, from what exists. By script: every item with dynamic, law, strength, family, base; a default kind for 79 of the 103 transitions from their 'kind' field (exact threshold, tipping in a parameter, critical mass become lines; window or deadline becomes moves with 'within'); the 160 witness exits become built cases; a candidate line wherever the cited Lean statement is an iff; items citing the same law grouped; overlap, containment, empty borders and the index table computed; the chart layout. By reading: the question list (nine here; my guess is 20 to 25 for all eight families, not tested); each place's answers (15 now, under 40 later, and mostly a rewrite of the existing tests); for each item 'on', 'kind' and 'given'. For the 88 the notes already say these in prose, so it is a pass over notes with one refuter, not over the Lean; for the other 346 it rides on the adjudication already planned. The exits' 'drops' field does not give the questions directly: 191 distinct premises are dropped across 321 exits and only 15 are shared by more than one dynamic, so a small table from premise to question is needed. Each actual case's answers: one exists.
scales_to_other_families:
Read: all 29 dynamics of A (Absorption and ending) and all 10 of E (Waiting and reciprocity), names, mechanisms' openings, exits and transitions; not their Lean.

A. Holds, with three stresses. Its 30 transitions are 11 windows or deadlines, 6 exact thresholds, 3 tippings, 3 exits by drift, 4 readings; 20 of its 40 exits are witnesses. So A is mostly lines and built cases, which the flat map would draw as arrows. Examples: margin-of-a-regime exit 1 (RegimeMargin.ends_iff_below, 'ends exactly where it starts below H + y') is a line on 'is the level above its point of no return' followed by 'on'. every-loss-passes-a-juncture is the general law of the region's own question 'time', so A adds marks to an existing question and no new place. three-outcomes-of-a-loss needs a three-answer question (restored, transformed, ended): allowed. Stresses: (i) deadlines need the 'within' count. (ii) The cascade laws (a-cascade-along-total-dependence, co-ending, a-whole-of-every-part) relate one thing's going on to another's along dependence; they fit as marks on 'on' with 'given' naming another role's answer, but their natural picture is the case's own web of who depends on whom, not the chart. (iii) attraction-is-not-returning, basins and necessarily-drawn say what staying, leaving and being drawn into a region mean for any process (Run.leaving_needs: leaving needs a move that does not keep the region). They are the legend of the map, the meaning of a stays mark and a moves mark, not places on it; a flat list would have to make them places. Also four-routes-of-transition (a reading) is already a list of kinds of change (a parameter change, a shock, a failure of correction, change too fast for correction); my four kinds should be reconciled with it and not coined beside it.

E. Holds for the comparisons, bends at the core. All 5 transitions are tippings in a parameter. offspring tr 1 and 2 (answering favoured exactly where γ ≤ β) are lines on the same question 'pays' with the practice being giving back, so E needs no twin of 'Bending the rule pays'; that is the scaling gain in one example. The core laws (restoring-giving-from-the-worst-start exits 1 and 2, Tolerance.restores_iff: gives at step n from every start exactly where no chain of n waits leads into it) are lines whose sides are a property of the shape of a web of waits. They can be stored as a question, but the chart cannot show a chain; the case sheet over the situation's web carries them.

Where it would break: if one family needs more than three live questions the chart must split into several sheets, and the families-by-questions index becomes the top-level map. That index is cheap and I think it is the true terrain. At 35 to 40 places the flat list grows by a place per new combination; here places stay names over about 20 to 25 questions (a guess) and the number drawn on any one sheet stays near a dozen.
first_change: Give every decision a 'kind' (line, stays, moves, re-set, built case, reading) and draw only 'moves' as a solid arrow: lines as a shared border or a double bar between the two boxes, re-sets as hollow arrows, built cases as dots. It needs no new place list and no new layout, it can be filled for the 88 from the notes already written, and it changes what a person takes from the present map in five minutes: the eight arrows into 'The cost counts' become no solid arrow at all, and the costs/pays pair becomes one border. The second change, which this one prepares, is the 'on' field: which question each mark is about, with places rewritten as sets of answers.
cost_to_build: For the first region: a list of nine questions and 15 places rewritten as answers (an hour or two of reading, then Ren's ear for the wording in both languages); three fields added to 88 decisions from their existing notes, one reader and one refuter; draw.py's node placement replaced by a grid computed from question order, panel and template kept. No Lean, no build, no gate. For the other families it adds three fields to the adjudication already under way, plus a premise-to-question table for the dropped premises (191 in all).
false_premise: Two, and one caution. (1) 'The data structure that projects onto the map' takes places and arrows to be the stored thing. They are already projections; the store underneath is distinctions and what laws say about each. Asking whether the place list is optimal is asking about a view. (2) 'Pareto frontier' supposes one drawing judged on fixed counts. The counts pull apart (five minutes against every limit visible), and a cartographer does not answer that with one best sheet but with levels of zoom over one store: an index, a chart per region, a panel per mark, the Lean statement. What can be shown by argument is only that a structure is dominated, which the present one is. Which sheet a person understands better in five minutes cannot be shown by a designer or by AI readers; it takes one person and two sheets. (Caution) 'Not dualistic' cannot be reached by structure alone: a chart read left to right will be read as better to the right unless the order is said to be the order in which the questions can be asked.
